security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI HSM context-save/restore or mideleg configuration iterates over known local interrupts (e.g., only codes 0-13) and fails to include interrupt code 14 (LAMBI), leaving its priority state in miprio/siprio CSR arrays unsaved across suspend/resume or its delegation unconfigured, while Ssamb hardware drives asynchronous memory buffer events.
security_spec.summary: New local interrupt 14 (LAMBI) adds CSR state in miprio/siprio priority arrays and mie/mideleg bits that OpenSBI HSM save/restore and delegation init must cover; stale or zeroed priority after context switch creates priority inversion or spurious M-mode trap races.

findings.finding: No IRQ_14 / IRQ_LAMBI constant defined. The highest defined local interrupt is IRQ_PMU_OVF=13. No MIP_LAMBI or SIP_LAMBI bit macro exists either. This is the root cause that prevents any other code path from correctly handling interrupt code 14.

mideleg is configured with interrupts = MIP_SSIP | MIP_STIP | MIP_SEIP | sbi_pmu_irq_mask(). sbi_pmu_irq_mask() returns BIT(13) for SSCOFPMF. Bit 14 (LAMBI) is never set in the delegation mask. If Ssamb hardware drives interrupt 14, it will trap to M-mode instead of being delegated to S-mode.

The switch statement handles IRQ_M_TIMER(7), IRQ_M_SOFT(3), IRQ_M_EXT(11), and PMU overflow(13). Interrupt code 14 (LAMBI) falls through to the default branch which returns SBI_ENOENT. In sbi_trap_handler() this triggers sbi_trap_error() → sbi_hart_hang(), permanently hanging the hart.

Same vulnerability as nonaia path: the switch statement processes IRQ_M_TIMER, IRQ_M_SOFT, IRQ_M_EXT, and PMU overflow. Interrupt 14 (LAMBI) falls to default → returns SBI_ENOENT → hart hang via sbi_trap_error(). The AIA path is equally affected.

After either trap IRQ handler returns SBI_ENOENT (which happens for interrupt 14), control reaches the trap_done label with msg="unhandled local interrupt", causing a call to sbi_trap_error() and ultimately sbi_hart_hang(). The hart is permanently dead.

HSM non-retentive suspend saves MIE, MIP (S-mode bits only), MEDELEG, MIDELEG, and MENVCFG, but does NOT save miprio/siprio CSR arrays. If interrupt priorities for code 14 were programmed differently from the cold-boot default, they will be lost across suspend/resume cycles. The struct sbi_hsm_data (line 44-53) has no field for these CSRs.

The restore path restores MENVCFG, MIDELEG, MEDELEG, MIE, MIP — but never restores miprio/siprio. After resume, the hart will have cold-boot default priority values, not the values configured before suspend.

struct hart_context saves/restores S-mode CSRs (sstatus, sie, stvec, sscratch, sepc, scause, stval, sip, satp, scounteren, senvcfg, srmcfg) for domain context switching but does not include siprio. If Ssamb hardware uses different interrupt priority settings across domains, those settings will leak or be clobbered on context switch.
